Facing the enemy, the Prophet led the fear prayer in two parties, one praying with him while the other stood guard, then changing; if outnumbered, pray standing or riding.
On the Dhat-ur-Riqa and Najd expeditions the Prophet leads the Fear Prayer with two batches in turn, and spares a bedouin who seized his sword as he slept.
In the fear prayer the imam leads each of two groups in one rak'a while the other faces the enemy; in great fear people may pray standing or riding.
